nodes.label: No loop guard republisher rule
nodes.rationale: A republisher subscribes to one exact source and channel of a device created earlier, so republish chains are finite and cannot close into a cycle.

nodes.label: HBRIDGE contract (0x09xx)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: Drive is an integer count of 12-bit PWM steps; the wire carries no floats so the driver gets full resolution. A contract, not a module with state, so ops mean the same on every motor driver.

nodes.label: sys_dev_pin_t take/drive/release helpers
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: An invalid pin (SYS_IO_PIN_NONE) is stored as NONE and does nothing so optional pins need no checks at the call site.

nodes.label: IO contract (0x01xx)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: Wrappers only build sys_device_call so an internal call and a remote command run the same code; unsupported ops answer ERR_DEV_UNKNOWN_OP.

nodes.label: SYS_IO_PIN_NONE encoding (device 0xFFFF)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: A zero-filled pin field is device 0 pin 0, a real pin, so unused needs an explicit non-zero encoding.

nodes.label: PINS contract (0x02xx, lock bookkeeping)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: A lock is bookkeeping, not identity: LOCK/UNLOCK senders are trusted, no owner ID in the contract.

nodes.label: LiPo battery estimate
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (

nodes.label: Power budget and rail rebalance
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: Budget = measured input mV x source mA capped by the board; fixed rails reserve first, automatic rails split the remainder; 64-bit products avoid overflow.

nodes.label: POWER_VREG guard (budget check on rail changes)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.norm_label: power_vreg guard (budget check on rail changes)
nodes.rationale: Single guard per contract; its own rail changes use sys_device_call_direct to avoid calling back into the guard. Lock order: guard takes sys_pwrm_mutex then calls devices directly.

nodes.label: Fault response matrix (NOTIFY/DISABLE/RESET/SAFE_STATE)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: One row per rail plus a board row so rail A can keep running while rail B is cut; saved as record SYS_ACTIONS_ID_POWER_RESPONSES.

nodes.label: Power source detection (USB/PSU/BATTERY/UNKNOWN)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (

nodes.label: POWER_MONITOR contract (0x04xx)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: GET_POWER falls back to sys_power_mW with an int64 product so 20 V x 5.5 A does not overflow.

nodes.label: POWER_SUPPLY contract (0x08xx, power mux)
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: Break-before-make: the active source is switched off, switch delay passes, then the new one on, so both are never on together.

nodes.label: POWER_USB_PD contract (0x07xx)

nodes.label: Bank-alternating atomic commit
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: A save fills the spare bank and the project record write is the commit point, so the stored project is never touched by a failed or aborted save.

nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (

nodes.label: Project run and boot autostart
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: RUN nests three levels (project record, chunk list, chunk) so SYS_ACTIONS_MAX_DEPTH must be >= 3; the VM start is the program's own last EXEC frame, the firmware does not know the VM here.

nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: One table per contract over one engine; a _Static_assert per row ties fields to the contract arg struct. Operation kinds CHANGE / EDGE / READ with optional idle op.

nodes.label: VM_BLOCK_TYPE_DEFINE registration and load-time verify
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: Shape checked once at load by vm_block_verify so bodies never re-check; component is WHOLE_ARCHIVE so nothing else references a block.

nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: Action is queued and run on the router task, not inside the pass, because an action may stop, rewind or unload the program and a long replay would outlast the block watchdog.

nodes.label: HBRIDGE fault response policy
nodes.community_name: VM_BLOCKS.MD (block palette  / Shared device block engine (
nodes.rationale: The driver decides the response (turn_off_at_ocp brakes the channel); events are NOTIFY because a fault must be seen by the user. No system-wide response, unlike the power manager.

nodes.label: Device block call semantics (setting / action / reading)
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.norm_label: device block call semantics (setting / action / reading)
nodes.rationale: Setting sent on first enabled pass and on change; action once per rising enable; reading every enabled pass. Device refuses what it cannot do, nothing is clamped.

nodes.label: Block palette registry
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Core knows no block; each block registers itself via VM_BLOCK_TYPE_DEFINE into g_vm_block_types[].

nodes.label: Per-pass event queue
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics

nodes.label: Program clock
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Time not running passes does not count, so debugging stops do not break timing blocks; step_ms is added per stepped pass.

nodes.label: Retained values (NVS)

nodes.label: Telemetry as router command
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Board writes values in the format the app writes them, so one decoder serves both directions and frames can be replayed.

nodes.label: For block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Max turns is a hard budget so a loop that would not end (step 0, wrong direction) cannot stall the pass.

nodes.label: If block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Both outputs are cleared every pass they are not taken so a block below never keeps running by accident.

nodes.label: Latch block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Turns a one-pass pulse into a held level, to remember that something happened.

nodes.label: On event block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Events are not consumed and live one pass; a disabled block misses them like a physical edge.

nodes.label: Every (periodic tick) block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Deadline advances by exactly one period so the rate does not drift; missed ticks are dropped, not replayed.

nodes.label: Set block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics

nodes.label: Switch block
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics

nodes.label: Timer block (IEC 61131-3)
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: A disabled timer is not skipped: it runs with a false signal so off-delay and pulse finish on their own.

nodes.label: Wire format never renumbered
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Router key, op numbers, vm_wire.h records, block type numbers and error tags are wire format; new ones go at the end.

nodes.label: Enable / ENO flow and freshness
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Not acting keeps outputs and drops ENO quietly; ENO true sets upd; freshness is cleared only by the supervisor at pass end (fan-out).

nodes.label: Loader fail-closed
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Any failing load op discards the whole program; nothing is rolled back piecemeal.

nodes.label: VM scan pass
nodes.community_name: vm_core spec (VM_CORE.MD) / Device block call semantics
nodes.rationale: Client sorts, the board never does: block ID is execution order; every block is called every pass and decides itself whether to act.

nodes.community_name: sys_event component (events) / INA3221 power monitor manual
nodes.norm_label: current computed from shunt voltage (i = v/r)
nodes.rationale: The chip has no current register, so range and resolution depend on the shunt resistor; a wrong shunt setting scales every reading.

nodes.label: SYS_EVENT_NOTIFY and SYS_EVENT_DEFER flags
nodes.community_name: sys_event component (events) / INA3221 power monitor manual
nodes.rationale: NOTIFY marks events that matter to the user and is set in the contract table, not by publishers; DEFER keeps listeners out of background tasks an op may wait for.
